title: Selvage Session Protocol — the version, capabilities and clocks a peer advertises
description: The wire version, the capability grammar, and the advertised block (`capabilities` plus `keepalive`) that both `GET /meta` and the reply to `session.hello` carry. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §2; the canonical byte form is CANONICAL.md §2.5.

wireVersion.description: The one wire version this protocol has, as a producer writes it: `selvage/2`. The `v` member of every text frame and the whole of `GET /meta`'s `wire_versions` carry it, and a receiver that reads anything else is reading a frame that is not this protocol's (CANONICAL.md §2.5).

capabilityName.description: A capability name. Unknown names are ignored by both sides and there is no failure mode for one a peer cannot honour (`NOTES.md` §B.9); there is therefore no schema that says a capability is mandatory.

keepalive.description: The session's clocks, advertised by the server. The advertised values are the session's: a client that substitutes its own disagrees with its peers about when a cursor is stale (§8.2, §9). `/meta`'s object carries `room_grace_ms` in addition to the three clocks the handshake reply also carries.

awareness_expire_ms.description: How long a client keeps a remote awareness state it has not seen renewed. A state not renewed inside this window will be forgotten, and the forgetting happens on the renewal tick, so it can arrive up to `awareness_renew_ms` late (§8.2).

awareness_renew_ms.description: How often a client republishes its own awareness state. It is also the clock a peer's holds lease is defined by: a hold not renewed inside a lease of the same length expires (§13.7).

ping_interval_ms.description: How often the server sends a WebSocket Ping. Protocol-level pings are not session messages and are never relayed (§9).

room_grace_ms.description: The server's default room grace period: how long a room survives its **last** connection ending (§9). Advertised in `GET /meta`'s `keepalive` (§2), and `/meta` is where a client reads it, because the connection that has to size its retry budget to the grace is the one that is gone. A client reads it to size its reconnect retry so that it does not give up inside a window the room still exists for (§9.1); the number is policy.

advertisedVersions.description: The versions a server accepts, in `GET /meta`. There is one version, so this is a list of one entry: the member stays a list, and a server that accepts nothing has no reason to answer.

metaKeepalive.description: The `keepalive` object `GET /meta` carries: the three clocks plus `room_grace_ms`, which only `/meta` has (PROTOCOL.md §2). A second `$def` rather than a member moved into `keepalive`, because the handshake reply carries the same object without it and a requirement there would be false.

capabilityList.description: An advertised capability list. Advertised additively and read additively: a peer ignores names it does not know, in `/meta` and in the handshake reply. Two names are this protocol's: `y-protocols/1` and `awareness`.
